take: Middle East chokepoint flows rose 19% in 3Q26, a reminder that physical supply routes remain concentrated and headline-sensitive even as agency reports flag a looming surplus, keeping crude in its narrow range and product cracks hostage to any disruption premium. On the shipping side, a bloody week in the Persian Gulf and around the Black Sea alongside Scotland’s consent for the 1GW Muir Mhòr floating wind farm and Seaway 7’s three-vessel Berwick Bank B deployment underline that tonne-miles are being reshaped by both conflict risk and offshore wind build-out, with the latter slowly displacing some fossil freight demand. The inventory angle is thin but pointed: US natural gas storage ended the injection season at 3,810 Bcf, almost 2% above the five-year average, capping upside for gas-linked power and indirectly for distillate demand into winter. Cross-market, watch the middle-distillate tilt in refinery yields against bunker economics, as high distillate and jet margins keep pulling barrels away from the bottom of the barrel whilst Alaskan crude output is forecast to grow 13% in 2027, adding medium-term length to US supply. Over the next 24 hours, track any escalation in Gulf or Black Sea shipping incidents and the House’s next move on the permitting bill, both of which could shift the balance between glut expectations and risk premium.

items.title: U.S. natural gas inventories end injection season above normal levels
items.summary: Working natural gas in storage in the Lower 48 states ended the natural gas injection season at 3,810 billion cubic feet (Bcf), exceeding the five-year average by almost 2%, according to estimates based on data from our Weekly Natural Gas Storage Report released on November 12. Injection season runs April 1–October 31, the months of typically lower natural gas demand.
